I will keep to the wheat-maize rotation that fits Quzhou County best. I farm on the North China Plain, so I value a system that is stable, mechanizable, and well matched to my soil, water, and market conditions. At my age, I do not want to spread myself across too many crops with different management needs. Because I am well educated, I am comfortable using improved seed, measured fertilizer application, and tighter field management instead of relying on habit alone.

I will start with winter wheat on my main land because it is the most dependable crop here and uses the full cool season well. I will manage it with improved seed, moderate nitrogen, balanced phosphorus and potassium, and a few key irrigations tied to jointing, booting, and grain filling if moisture is short. I will use rotary tillage because it is efficient and suits residue handling and local machinery. I will keep pesticide sprays limited to the periods when disease, aphids, or weeds justify them.

After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize on the same land. I will use hybrid seed because the yield advantage is worth it for maize here. I will feed maize more nitrogen than wheat, keep phosphorus and potassium balanced, and irrigate only when rainfall is not enough, since summer rain usually carries part of the load. I will stay with rotary tillage or a light seedbed approach after wheat so I can plant quickly and protect the season length. My goal is a simple, strong annual system: wheat for stability, maize for output, careful input control, and no unnecessary complexity.
